case_name: Jun et al v. Wantell Business Networks & Zang
text:
Citation:

Jun et al v. Wantell
Business Networks & Zang

Date:

20081104

2008 BCPC 0321

File No:

06-11946

Registry:

Vancouver

IN THE PROVINCIAL COURT OF BRITISH
COLUMBIA

BETWEEN:

LIU JUN et al

CLAIMANTS

AND:

WANTELL BUSINESS NETWORKS
CORPORATION

& ANDREW ZANG

DEFENDANTS

PRE-TRIAL
RULING

OF
THE

HONOURABLE
JUDGE PHILLIPS

Appearing for the Claimants:

Casey
Smith (Student-at-Law, LSLAP - UBC)

Appearing for the Defendant
Wantell:

Don
MacLean (Communications Director)

Appearing on his own behalf and
for Wantell (Program Advisor & Director):

Andrew
Zang

Place of Hearing:

Vancouver,
B.C.

Date of Hearing:

October
21, 2008

Date of Judgment:

November 4, 2008

HISTORY OF LITIGATION

[
1
]
The Claimants are involved in twenty-six similar claims for return of tuition
fees and loss of wages against Wantell Business Networks Corp. (carrying on
business as City Tech College).  In some of the proceedings, claims have
also been brought against Andrew Zang, the President of
Wantell.   This is the decision of the Court on Applications brought
by some of the Claimants to add Zang as a personal defendant.  The Court
has also heard an Application by the Defendant Zang to dismiss the claims
already brought against him in his personal capacity.

[
2
]
These cross-applications came before me as the Administrative Judge dealing
with all twenty-six claims in a case management capacity.   The
parties did not take issue with the authority of the Court to rule on these
applications at this stage.  I am satisfied that the interests of justice
are served on these voluminous Small Claims matters by addressing these
pre-trial applications now.

[
3
]
The Claimants are all Chinese students who claim they responded to advertizing
by Wantell in 2005 regarding B.C. student loan and grant funds being available
to use to attend the College.  In their Notices of Claim, the student
state they dealt with Zang, Wynston Chen, Jennifer Wu and possibly other unnamed
staff of Wantell.  Based on information they received regarding their
ability to qualify for loan funding and about Mandarin language instruction (or
assistance), they applied for funding and enrolled in the College.  All of
the Claimants allege they were later audited by the BC Student loan program and
determined to be ineligible for the loans.   For the most part, the
students allege Wantell representatives had them declare their four or more
years of university education in China at only twenty months for the purposes
of the student loans.  When the true extent of their Chinese education was
discovered the government deemed the Claimants to be ineligible and demanded
the loan money be repaid.

[
4
]
Although the Notices of Claim vary somewhat, in the majority the Claimants
allege they were mislead by the misrepresentations of Wantell officials
regarding student loan qualifications and claim they would not have applied for
the loan money and enrolled with the College but for the misrepresentations.
More particularly, the Claimants variously allege that Zang was actively
involved in the day-to-day administration of the College and was managing its
affairs throughout.  The students claim against Zang in his personal
capacity as President in that he gave misleading information to the Claimants
about the loans upon which they relied.

[
5
]
The history of the twenty-six individual claims relative to the role of Zang is
set out below.  For a significant period of time during which the cases
have been before the courts, little has happened on the files.  In
thirteen cases where Amended Notices of Claim adding Zang as a defendant were
filed prior to Settlement Conference, the cases stalled principally due to the
difficulties the Claimants apparently experienced in personally serving
Zang.  Throughout the time period in question, Wantell has been
represented by legal counsel who was apparently aware of the Amended Notices
and the allegations against the President of the Company.

[
6
]
At Pre-Trial Conferences held earlier this year, this Court concluded that it
would be very difficult to try all twenty-six cases together in that the trial
would become extremely lengthy and the scheduling of witnesses very
cumbersome.

[
7
]
Accordingly, the Court invited submissions from the parties in an effort to
identify a “lead” case which would then proceed to trial.  On July 8,
2008, the Court ordered that 0611946
Liu Jun v. Wantell and Andrew
Zang
proceed to trial first.  Although the court ordered that counsel
attend at the Judicial Case Manager’s office to schedule a three day hearing
for the end of 2008, that apparently did not happen.  At the conclusion of
this hearing on October 21
st
, the parties were again directed to set
a three day hearing with the trial coordinator.  The case has now been
scheduled for trial April 7 through 9, 2009.

[
8
]
At this Pre-Trial Conference on October 21
st
, 2008, the Defendants
Wantell and Zang appeared for the first time without counsel.  They sought
an adjournment of the hearing of the applications relating to the addition of
Zang as a defendant in order that they might review the Claimants’ materials
and retain counsel.   The Claimants had filed written materials as
directed by the Court for the purposes of the Application but were unable to
serve the Defendants as the address for service on file was no longer
accurate.  The Defendants had prepared for the Application in that they
had filed their own written materials in relation to the matter.

[
9
]
The Court ordered that the Claimants proceed with their submissions on the
Application and then granted the Defendants an extended lunch break to
familiarize themselves with the Claimants’ written materials.  Given the
length of time these matters have been before the Court and the fact the
Defendants have had the benefit of counsel until very recently, the Court
declined the Defendants’ request for an adjournment and the Court heard
submissions on the cross-applications from both MacLean and Zang.

[
10
]
It should be noted that during this hearing the Court invited Zang and Wantell
to provide current addresses for service but Zang maintained he could only
offer the address of the home of a friend where he claimed to be
residing.  When pressed as to where he could be located during business
hours, he would not answer the Court’s question.  At the Court’s behest,
Zang later provided a business address for service where he told the Court a
staff person would be available to accept service of materials for the Defendants
during regular business hours.  Upon confirmation that the staff person
would notify Wantell and Zang of service of any materials, the Court directed
that the Claimants be permitted to personally serve Zang substitutionally
without further court order by leaving the documents with the receptionist at
the business address provided.

[
11
]

FILE SUMMARY

Claims in which Zang was
added as a party before a Settlement Conference (pursuant to Rule 8(1)(a)

a)

0611943
Xue Mei Zheng
v. Wantell & Zang

[
12
]
The Notice of Claim was filed in this case on April 28, 2006 against Wantell
for tuition monies and loss of wages.  The Notice alleges Wantell made
misrepresentations in providing incorrect information to the Claimant (through
her husband
He Pei Huang
) and then to the Government via College
counselor Jennifer [Wu].  Jennifer is said to have pressured the husband
by saying the student loan assistance opportunity would soon end and had the
husband sign a blank application form.  Jennifer said she would complete
the balance of the application on behalf of the Claimant.   When the
Claimant found employment and told Wantell she wanted to withdraw, the College
refused to refund her student loan money.  The Claimant was told by the
Government she would have to repay the money.

[
13
]
Wantell filed a Reply on May 15, 2006 denying the misrepresentations and
stating the Claimant did not withdraw from the program so to entitle her to a
full refund.  Wantell also Counterclaimed for the balance owing on the
contract.

[
14
]
An Amended Notice of Claim was filed June 20, 2006 adding Andrew Zang (and
others) as a defendants but without any substantive changes to the claim.
On August 28, 2006, a further amended Notice of Claim was filed with no
apparent changes.

[
15
]
In an Affidavit filed in relation to the Application herein, the Claimant
deposed that after applying to and being accepted by Wantell, she changed her
mind upon arrival in Canada.  When she asked the school for her money
back, the school would not return the funds. The Claimant ultimately did not
attend the College.

b)

0611944
Yong Liu
v. Wantell & Zang

[
16
]
This Notice of Claim was filed April 28, 2006 claiming tuition fees and “loss
of money”.  The Claimant alleges he spoke to Zang by phone and was told
the College taught courses in Chinese throughout the academic year and
encouraged the Claimant to apply for a student grant.  The Claimant states
he spoke with a College counselor (Jennifer) and was told he would qualify for
loan money despite his high level of education in China.  The Claimant was
later audited and learned he did not qualify for the loan.  When he
withdrew from the College, his request for a refund was refused.

[
17
]
A Reply was filed by Wantell on May 12, 2006 with a Counterclaim for monies
owing on the contract.

[
18
]
An Amended Notice of Claim was filed pursuant to Rule 8(1)(a) on June 21, 2006
adding Zang and Shelly Pan as defendants without any substantive
amendments.  On September 30, 2008 the claim was withdrawn as against Pan
only (on all files before the Court).

c)

0612027
Yan Liang
v. Wantell & Zang

[
19
]
The Notice of Claim was filed on May 4, 2006 claiming against Wantell for
tuition fees and loss of wages.    The Claimant alleges she
spoke to Zang about financial aid and he told her Wantell had special staff
(Wynston Chen, Marketing Manager) whose job it was to help applicants with
their loan applications.  The Claimant met with Chen to complete the
application and later received a student loan.  After being audited, the
Claimant was required to re-pay some of the loan money.  The Claimant is
the wife of Claimant Weibo
Deng
[see below].

[
20
]
A Reply was filed by Wantell on May 18, 2006 denying any misrepresentation and
Counterclaiming for monies owing.  An Amended Notice of Claim was filed on
June 20, 2006 adding Zang and Pan as Defendants without any substantive
amendments.

[
21
]
In an affidavit filed on this application, the Claimant deposed that she met
with Zang and told him she had a five year degree from China and that Zang told
her she would definitely get loan money in BC.   She recollected the
meeting with Zang lasted between 30 and 60 minutes and that she then met with
Wynston Chen.

d)

0612026
Wei Bo Deng v.
Wantell & Zang

[
22
]
The Notice of Claim was filed May 4, 2006 for tuition fees and loss of wages
due to misrepresentations made by Zang.  A Reply and Counterclaim was
filed on May 18, 2006.  An Amended Notice of Claim was filed on June 20,
2006 adding Zang and Pan as Defendants but without any substantive changes.

[
23
]
In an affidavit filed in relation to this application, the Claimant said he met
with Zang and that as a result Zang would have known of his education in
China.  He was told by Zang that he would qualify for a student
loan.  He recollected the meeting with Zang lasted 30 to 60 minutes and
that afterward he met with Wynston Chen.  He said he never saw or signed a
loan application and that he understood Chen had his wife sign the
documentation.

e)

0611913
Wei Jie Wang
v. Wantell & Zang

[
24
]
This Notice of Claim was filed on April 27, 2006 claiming for tuition fees and
loss of wages.   The Claimant alleges she spoke with Zang and told
him about her educational background in China and received certain guarantees
regarding student loans.  The Claimant alleges Wynston Chen assisted her
to complete the application form and she received information about quantifying
her time in school in China.  Upon being audited, the Claimant learned she
was not qualified and was asked to re-pay her loan.

[
25
]
A Reply was filed by Wantell on May 11, 2006 denying responsibility and
counterclaiming for the balance owing on the contract.

[
26
]
An Amended Notice of Claim was filed pursuant to Rule 8 on June 20, 2006 adding
Zang and Pan as defendants without any other amendments.  A further
amended Notice of Claim was filed June 21, 2006 without any apparent
changes.

f)

0612029
Zhang Na
v. Wantell & Zang

[
27
]
The Notice of Claim was filed on May 4, 2006 for tuition fees; loss of wages
and living costs incurred during study.  The Claimant’s husband,
Lifeng
Wei
, spoke with Zang on the phone and the next day husband and wife met
with Zang and then with Jennifer.   The Claimant states Zang mislead
her and her husband into making a false application for a student
loan.   Upon the advice Wantell gave to her husband, the husband
transferred a car into another person’s name so that he would qualify for a
student loan.

[
28
]
A Reply was filed by Wantell on May 18, 2006 denying responsibility and
Counterclaiming for monies owning on the contract.   A detailed Reply
to the Counterclaim was filed May 30, 2006.

[
29
]
An Amended Notice of Claim was filed on June 14, 2006 adding Zang and Shu Li as
defendants.  A further Amended Notice of Claim was filed on June 21, 2006
adding Shelly Pan as a defendant.

[
30
]
In an affidavit filed in this application, the Claimant deposed that Zang told
her that her Chinese educational background was not a problem and that she
should quickly apply for a student loan.  She attested that Zang completed
the forms with her

and her
husband and told them it was okay to say they had twenty months of background
education.

g)

0612028
Li Feng Wei
v. Wantell & Zang

[
31
]
This Notice of Claim was filed on May 4, 2006 seeking tuition fees and wage
loss (this Claimant is the husband of Claimant
Na Zhang)
. The Notice
alleges the Claimant called Wantell in response to a newspaper ad for free
education and that the Claimant spoke with Zang when he called.  Zang
emphasized the College program was guaranteed to lead to a good job in Canada
and that the government covered all of the costs.  The next day the
Claimant and his wife met with Zang who directed them to Jennifer Wu who filled
in the required forms.  The Claimant alleges that during the application
process Zang encouraged him to transfer his vehicle to another person so to
qualify for a student loan. The Claimant alleges that due to misleading
information from Zang, he and his wife enrolled with Wantell in error in
that  they understood their Chinese education would be considered to be
the equivalent of twenty months for the purpose of the application when the BC
Government would not in fact quantify it that way.

[
32
]
On May 18, 2006 a Reply was filed by Wantell denying liability and
Counterclaiming for the balance of tuition.  An amended Notice of Claim
was filed on June 14, 2006 adding Zang and  Shu Li as Defendants.  On
June 21, 2006 a further amended Notice was filed claiming against Shelly Pan.

[
33
]
In an affidavit filed in this application, the Claimant deposed that he spoke
with Zang by phone and advised Zang that he was an MBA graduate from China and
was told by Zang there was no problem with that fact.   Zang told him
his Chinese schooling would only be credited at twenty months and that he
should hurry and apply for a BC Student Loan.  Wei deposed that “Jennifer”
at the College completed the loan forms.

h)

0612173
Miao Lian Zhang
v. Wantell & Zang

[
34
]
This Notice of Claim was filed on May 15, 2006 claiming for tuition fees and
loss of wages due to misrepresentation (but not naming Zang).  A Reply
with Counterclaim was filed May 18, 2006.

[
35
]
An Amended Notice of Claim was filed on June 14, 2006 adding Zang but without
any substantive changes.  A further Amended Notice of Claim was filed June
21, 2006 without any substantive amendments.

i)

0611914
Min Wu
v. Wantell

& Zang

[
36
]
A Notice of Claim was filed on April 27, 2006 claiming for tuition fees and
loss of wages based on guarantees provided by Zang regarding the student
loans.  A Reply and Counterclaim was filed on May 11, 2006.  An
Amended Notice of Claim was filed June 20, 2006 adding Zang and Pan as
Defendants but without any substantive amendments.  This document was
re-filed on June 21, 2006.

j)

0611941
Jia You v.
Wantell & Zang

[
37
]
This Notice of Claim was filed on April 28, 2006 claiming for tuition fees,
loss of salary, and for daycare and transportation costs due to reliance on
misrepresentations by Wantell counselor Jennifer.  A Reply was filed on
May 12, 2006.

[
38
]
An Amended Notice of Claim was filed on April 28, 2006 changing the monetary
amounts claimed.  A further Amended Notice of Claim was filed on June 21,
2006 adding Zang and Pan as Defendants but without any substantive changes.

[
39
]
In her affidavit filed herein, the Claimant deposed she spoke with Zang
regarding whether she would qualify for a student loan.   She said
Jennifer told her that she would qualify.   The Claimant later tried
to withdraw from the College but was unable to get her money back.

k)

0611955
Xiang Yuan Luo v.
Wantell & Zan
g

[
40
]
The Notice of Claim was filed on May 1, 2006 for tuition fees and loss of wages
alleging misrepresentations by Zang.  The Reply was filed on May 30,
2006.  An Amended Notice of Claim was filed June 20, 2006 adding Zang as a
Defendant without any substantive amendments.

l)

0611916
Qiong Chen v.
Wantell & Zang

[
41
]
The Notice of Claim was filed on  April 27, 2006 claiming for tuition
fees, loss of wages, punitive damages for misrepresentation (by Zang and Chen),
breach of contract and breaches of the
Business Practices and Consumer
Protection Act
.   A Reply was

filed on May 11,
2006.  An Amended Notice of Claim was filed on April 27, 2006 adding Zang
and Pan as Defendants but without any substantive amendments.

m)

0611946
Liu Jun v.
Wantell & Jun Zang
* (Set For Trial)

[
42
]
This Notice of Claim was filed on April 28, 2006 for tuition fees and loss of
wages based on misrepresentations by Zang.  The Reply was filed on May 12,
2006.  An Amended Notice of Claim was filed on June 21, 2006 adding Zang
and Pan but without any substantive amendments.

[
43
]
In an affidavit filed herein, the Claimant attested she told Zang over the
phone that she had a Masters Degree from China and was told by Zang that she
would qualify for BC Student Loan money.  She said Jennifer filled out the
loan form.  The Claimant deposed that Zang pressured her husband to sign a
blank loan application form and that Zang would not refund her husband’s money
when he asked the College for it back.

Claims
in which Andrew Zang has been added in compliance with the Rules or by Order of
the Court

n)

0509811
Hua Zhang
v. Wantell & Zang

[
44
]
This Notice of Claim was filed on November 18, 2005 against Wantell for return
of tuition fees based on misrepresentation by a Wantell counselor regarding the
Claimant’s qualifying training in China, and damages for loss of wages, or
rescission.  In an affidavit filed at this Application, the Claimant
deposed that he met with Zang and Wynston Chen for the purposes of his student
loan application.

[
45
]
A Reply filed by Wantell on November 30, 2005 denies any misrepresentation and
Counterclaims for unpaid tuition.  At a Settlement Conference heard on
April 11, 2006, the Counterclaim was dismissed.

[
46
]
On June 6, 2006 the Claimant filed an ex parte application to add Zang as a
defendant on the basis that he was the President of the Company and “did many
misleading, deceiving in this case…” and over concerns the company might become
bankrupt.   On June 7, 2006 a further application to add Zang was
filed.  On July 11, 2006 Ehrcke, J. ordered that Zang be added as a
defendant and that the Claimant have leave to file an amended Notice of Claim
and serve it substitutionally on that date.

[
47
]
An Amended Notice of Claim was filed on August 14, 2006 pursuant to Ehrcke,
J.’s order of July 11, 2006.  Other than the addition of Zang, no
amendments were made to the Notice.  On July 9th, 2008 the Amended Notice
of Claim was dismissed as a nullity for non-compliance with Judge Ehrcke’s
order.

o)

0509810
Wen Xin (David) Xue & Ying (Teresa)

Ke
v.
Wantell & Zang

[
48
]
This Notice of Claim was filed on November 18, 2005 claiming tuition and loss
of wages for each Claimant.  The Claimants allege they met with Jennifer
at the College and, with her assistance, filled out the student loan
application forms.   The Claimants allege they were told their
Chinese education would be discounted for loan purposes.

[
49
]
A Reply was filed by Wantell on November 30, 2006 and a Settlement Conference
heard on April 11, 2006.

[
50
]
An Order was made on June 20, 2006 by Pendleton, J. that the Claimants were at
liberty to add Zang and Pan as defendants.  An Amended Notice of Claim was
filed on June 21, 2006 pursuant to this Order adding Zang and Pan as
Defendants.   A further order was made on November 7, 2006 by
Pendleton, J. for substitutional service of the Amended Notice of Claim on Zang
and Pan.

Claims
in which amended pleadings have been filed following a ruling by Judge Mondin

p)

0611084
He Pei Huang
v. Wantell

[
51
]
This Notice of Claim was filed on February 24, 2006 claiming for tuition fees
and for loss of wages.  The Claimant says he was pressed by a Wantell
counselor to apply for a student loan and that the counselor primarily
completed the loan form.  A Reply was filed on March 10, 2006 denying
liability.  A Settlement Conference was held before Judge Rae on June 5,
2006.

[
52
]
On July 4, 2006 Ehrcke, J. adjourned an Application to amend the
pleadings.  On August 1, 2006 Ehrcke, J. again adjourned the Application
to amend pleadings to a two hour hearing.

[
53
]
On October 3, 2006 Mondin, J. ruled on the Application:  “the matter is
adjourned generally.  The Claimant is to provide an affidavit in support
of the application to a Judge together with a proposed amended Notice of
Claim.”  At the conclusion of the transcript of this hearing, counsel for
Wantell summarized Judge Mondin's order as follows (with approval of the
Court):

And to
confirm, then, Your Honour, there will be an order that the matters are
adjourned generally, and to be brought back on notice, pursuant to the rules,
with affidavits in support of the applications, applications to a judge
themselves, and proposed Amended Notices of Claim? Is that right?

[
54
]
On June 15
th
, 2007 an Amended Notice of Claim was filed with a
handwritten notation stating:  “Amended by request of Judge Mondin on
October 3, 2006 pursuant to Rule 8(1)(b)”.  The amendment adds Zang as a
Defendant.  The Amended document includes substantive additions regarding
alleged misrepresentations by Zang.

[
55
]
In an Affidavit filed June 26
th
, 2008 the Claimant’s reasons for
wanting to add Zang as a Defendant are detailed.    The Claimant
states Zang was actively involved with the College and counselled applicants
regarding completion of student loan forms and made representations regarding
loan availability and language of instruction.

[
56
]
In a further affidavit filed on his own behalf along with that of his wife, the
Claimant deposed that he worked with Jennifer in filling out the student loan
forms and had no interaction with Zang.  He attests both he and his wife
later changed their schooling plans and that he was able to have the Wantell
funds applied to another school.  He alleges his wife’s loan monies were
kept by Zang and Chen.

[
57
]
A Draft Amended but unfiled Notice of Claim provided to the Court pleads
misrepresentation and, alternatively, breaches of the
Business Practices and
Consumer Protection Act
, specifically deceptive acts or practices and
unconscionable acts or practices; and in the further alternative, breach of
fiduciary duty.

q)

0611082
Mei-Lin Tang
v. Wantell

[
58
]
This Notice of Claim was filed on February 26, 2006 claiming tuition fees and
loss of wages.   The Claimant states that in response to a newspaper
ad she attended the College and met with a counselor, applied for and obtain a
student loan.  A Reply filed March 10, 2006 denies the claim and seeks
unpaid tuition by way of a Counterclaim.   The case has the same
history as
0611084
(above) regarding Mondin, J.’s order.

[
59
]
On June 15
th
, 2007 an Amended Notice of Claim was filed “as per
order of Judge Mondin on October 3, 2006”.  The amendment includes
substantive amendments to the Notice relating to Zang’s misrepresentations.

[
60
]
In an affidavit filed at this Application, the Claimant attests that she relied
on Wynston Chen for the student loan process but makes no allegations against
Zang.

r)

0509543
Han Ma
v. Wantell

[
61
]
This Notice of Claim was filed on November 1, 2005 claiming for tuition fees,
wage loss, and for punitive, exemplary and/or aggravated damages.  The
Notice does not make allegations relating to the student loan process, but
alleges misrepresentation, breach of the
Business Practices and Consumer
Protection Act,
and breach of contract. In an affidavit filed for this
Application, the Claimant attests she received assurances from both Zang and
Chen.

[
62
]
The Reply filed November 10, 2005 denies the claim and makes a Counterclaim for
unpaid tuition and defamation.

[
63
]
On April 4, 2006 a Settlement Conference was held before Werier, J.  On
June 14, 2006, Romilly, J. adjourned a pre-trial conference pending an
application to add a defendant and ordered Ma to pay $100 costs to Wantell
before another pre-trial was set.

[
64
]
An Amended Notice of Claim was filed on June 15, 2007 per "Mondin J.’s
order" and alleging misrepresentation by Zang.

s)

0611939
Zhu Shu Lei
v. Wantell

[
65
]
The Notice of Claim was filed on April 28, 2006 claiming for tuition fees and
loss of wages.  The Claimant alleges Zang and Jennifer provided misleading
information regarding the student loan process.  The Reply filed on May
12, 2006 denies responsibility and makes a Counterclaim for an unpaid balance
on account.

[
66
]
On October 3, 2006, before Mondin, J., the Application to add Zang as a
Defendant was “Struck from the list”.

t)

0612042
Tao Huang v.
Wantell

[
67
]
The Notice of Claim was filed on May 5, 2006 for tuition fees and loss of wages
based on misrepresentations made by College counselor, Jennifer.  The
Reply was filed on June 6, 2006.  In an affidavit filed herein, the
Claimant deposed that Jennifer helped her with the loan application process and
that Zang reneged on a deal for reduced tuition fees.

[
68
]
On October 3, 2006, Mondin, J. adjourned generally an Application to amend the
pleadings.  The Claimant was directed to provide an affidavit in support
of the Application together with a proposed amended Notice of Claim.

u)

0611945

Yi Rong v. Wantell

[
69
]
The Notice of Claim was filed on April 28, 2006 for tuition fees and loss of
wages based on misrepresentations regarding student loans made by a College
counselor.  The Reply was filed on May 12, 2006.

[
70
]
On October 3, 2006, Mondin, J. considered an application to amend the pleadings
and adjourned the matter generally for the Claimant to provide an affidavit in
support and a proposed amended Notice.

[
71
]
An Amended Notice of Claim was filed on June 15, 2007 adding Zang “pursuant to
Mondin, J’s order” and with substantive amendments regarding the role of
Zang.

[
72
]
In an affidavit filed herein, the Claimant attests she met with Zang and
provided him information and then she met with Chen.  She said Chen’s
involvement was limited to having her sign the BC Student Loan application.

Cases
where Yee, J. dismissed applications to add Zang as a defendant

v)

0611083
Qun Yu
v.

Wantell

[
73
]
This Notice of Claim was filed on February 24, 2006 claiming tuition fees and
loss of wages and asserting Zang and Wynston Chen made
misrepresentations.  A

Reply filed on March 10,
2006 denies the claim and Counterclaims for monies unpaid on the contract.

[
74
]
On June 5, 2006 a Settlement Conference was held before Rae, J.  On
October 3, 2006 Mondin, J. struck an Application to amend pleadings from the
list.   On June 26, 2007 Yee, J. ruled on the Application to add Zang
and dismissed same.

w)

0611940
Feng Jun Cui
v. Wantell

[
75
]
This Notice of Claim was filed on April 28, 2006 claiming for tuition fees and
loss of wages.  The Claimant alleges Zang and Jennifer misrepresented
student loan and language of instruction matters.  The Reply was filed on
May 12, 2006 denying the claim.  On October 3, 2006 Mondin, J. struck the
matter from the list.  On June 26, 2007, before Yee, J., “by consent
application [to add Zang] withdrawn”.

x)

0509992
Hong Gang Hao
v. Wantell

[
76

LAW

Authority to consider
this Application

[
80
]
As noted at the outset of this decision, all of the parties here urged the
Court to find it had jurisdiction to consider the cross-applications at this
pre-trial stage.  The
Small Claims Act and Rules
are the
governing legislation for this Court.

[
81
]
The
Small Claims Act
RSBC 1996 chapter 430 sets out this guiding
purpose for the Court (in section 2):

(1)
The purpose of this Act and the rules is to allow people who bring claims to
the Provincial Court to have them resolved and to have enforcement proceedings
concluded in a just, speedy, inexpensive and simple manner.

(2)
Subject to this Act and the rules, in conducting a hearing the Provincial Court
may make any order or give any direction it thinks necessary to achieve the
purpose of this Act and the rules.

[
82
]

Small Claims Rule 16
provides for applications to be made to a judge at
a hearing and sets out orders which a judge may make upon such an application
being brought.  Rule 16(6) does not specifically address applications for
an order to dismiss a claim.  Rule 16(6)(o) provides that a judge may make
“any other order that a judge has the power to make and notice of which is
served on another party.”   The Court must be cautious not to expand
the application of Rule 16 beyond the specified matters unless the
circumstances involved make it appropriate to use the broad jurisdiction
provided for under Rule 16(6)(o) in reference to Section 2 of the
Act.

[
83
]
Rule 17(13) of the Small Claims Rules provides:

A party who
thinks that another party has not obeyed these rules may apply to a judge under
Rule 16(7) or at a hearing, and the judge may make any order or give any
direction that the judge thinks is fair.

[
84
]
In the circumstances herein, I am satisfied that the Court has the discretion
to hear an application to dismiss under Rule 16 (see also paragraph 13
Belanger
v. AT & T Canada Inc.

1994 B.C.J. No. 2792
Stansfield, J. as he then
was).

Amending Pleadings

[
85
]

Small Claims Rule 8(1)
provides:

Anything in a notice of claim, reply or other document that has been filed by a
party may be changed by that party

(a) without any permission, at any time before the settlement conference
begins, and

(b) with the permission of a judge (see Rule 16(7)), at any time after that.

[
86
]

Rule 8(3)
provides that a party who changes a filed document must file
and serve a copy of the revision.

[
87
]
Some guidance can be taken from BC Supreme Court Rule 15 addressing the matter
of adding a party to a proceeding.  Rule 15(5)(a) states:

(5)
(a)    At any stage of a
proceeding, the court on application by any person may

(i)
order that a party, who is not or has ceased to be a proper or necessary party,
cease to be a party,

(ii)
order that a person, who ought to have been joined as a party or whose
participation in the proceeding is necessary to ensure that all matters in the
proceeding may be effectually adjudicated upon, be added or substituted as a
party, and

(iii)
order that a person be added as a party where there may exist, between the
person and any party to the proceeding, a question or issue relating to or
connected

(A)
with any relief claimed in the proceeding, or

(B)
with the subject matter of the proceeding,

which in the
opinion of the court it would be just and convenient to determine as between
the person and that party.

[
88
]
The law thus provides that a court can add a party where to do so is in the
interests of justice and where necessary to ensure that all matters in the case
be effectually adjudicated.

,

[1990] 2 S.C.R. 959

Sigurdson, J. also noted the following regarding liability of directors (@

In

She concluded that, in the circumstances before her,

in the case before her, the particulars of negligence alleged against the

4  (1) If an action to which this or any other Act applies has been

ANALYSIS

[
97
]
Turning to the twenty-six claims herein, the Court must consider the
allegations against Zang in his personal capacity.   In a general
sense, the Claimants allege that Zang made negligent or fraudulent
misrepresentations to them and that they relied on those representations to
their detriment.   The Claimants argue that Zang may be personally
liable as his actions were tortious or exhibited a separate interest from
Wantell.

[
98
]
As noted above, the threshold of sustainability of pleadings is very low (per
Montreal
Trust Co.
supra
@ paragraph 39).   Many of the Notices of
Claim filed originally included claims against Zang for what he allegedly
misrepresented the availability of student loan funding and Chinese language
instruction to be.  From those early claims, Zang would have known at the
outset of this litigation that the Claimants were making allegations against him
in terms of his personal involvement with some of the Claimants.  Although
I am mindful that much time has passed since the impugned conduct was said to
have occurred, in the circumstances I am unable to find any prejudice to Zang
by allowing the claims to proceed nor was one advanced other than the passage
of time.  Zang himself must bear some of the burden of the delay in that
he was both unavailable at times to be served and unavailable to participate in
court proceedings.   In that he did not fulfill his obligation to the
Court to provide a proper address for personal service to be effected, his own
conduct made it difficult for the Claimants to prosecute their claims.

[
99
]
Although the law is clear that officers of a company, such as Zang, who are the
directing minds of the company have the same identity of interests as the
corporation and thus the same immunity, I am not prepared to dismiss the
actions against Zang at this stage in those cases where the Claimants have put
forward claims that Zang made misrepresentations to them.   In the
group of thirteen claims where Zang was added as a Defendant prior to a
Settlement Conference, where the Claimants allege Zang directly mislead the
Claimants, Zang will remain as a Defendant.   Those eleven claims
are:

- Yong Liu
(0611944)

- Yan Liang (0612027)

- Wei Jie Wang (0611913)

- Zhang Na (0612029)

- Min Wu (0611914)

- Jia You (0611941)

- Wei Bo Deng (0612026)

- Xiang Yuan Luo (0611955)

- Qiong Chen
(0611916)

- Liu Jun (0611946)

- Li Feng Wei
(0612028)

However, in the
remaining two cases in this group of thirteen claims (0611943 Xue Mei Zheng and
0612173 Miao Lian Zhang) no reference is made against Zang in his personal
capacity in the pleadings or affidavit material.  Thus I direct that on
these two cases, the claims only go forward now against the corporate
Defendant, Wantell.

[
100
]
In the matter of Wen Xin (David) Xue and Ying (Teresa) Ke (0509810), Pendleton,
J. has previously ordered that Zang be added as a Defendant.   I
think it would be improper for this Court to revisit this issue and direct that
this Claim proceed against Zang.

[
101
]
In the case of Hua Zhang (0509811), the Amended Notice of Claim was dismissed
as a nullity earlier in these proceedings.  No new application has been
brought to add Zang as a Defendant nor has any appeal been taken against the
ruling declaring the Amendment a nullity.  Accordingly, on this claim, the
action now may only be prosecuted as against the Corporate Defendant, Wantell.

[
102
]
The clearest case in terms of these cross-applications is 0611083 (Qun Yu)
which was dealt with by Judge Yee on June 26, 2007.  On that date Judge
Yee considered an Application to add Zang as a defendant and, having examined
the claim, the Application was dismissed.  The Court has already ruled
against the amended Notice of Claim and the only remedy available to the
Claimant was to have taken an appeal of Judge Yee’s decision.  No
Application has been brought to pursue the matter further against Zang
personaly and, accordingly, this claim will carry on as against the Corporate
Defendant, Wantell, only.

[
103
]
On the four other cases before Judge Yee, on June 26, 2007, Applications to add
Zang as a Defendant were withdrawn by consent.   At this hearing, the
Claimants have brought new Applications to add Zang.  In all four of these
cases allegations are made that Zang made misrepresentations in his personal
capacity.  I find that it would be in the interests of justice to allow
the claims to go forward against both Wantell and Zang.
Accordingly, on 0611940 (Feng Jun Cui), 0509992 (Hong Gang Hao), 0611942 (Li
Li) and 0611388 (Yang Cui), I allow the Claimants’ Applications to add Zang as
a Defendant.

[
104
]
Finally, in the last six cases where Judge Mondin directed that the
Applications to add Zang proceed in a certain fashion, the record is clear that
the Claimants did not follow the process of the Court for adding Zang as
required by Judge Mondin.    The reasons for the Claimants not
following the direction of the Court are unclear.  However, these
cross-applications put the issue of Zang’s status as a party clearly and fully before
the Court.

[
105
]
In two of the claims which Judge Mondin adjourned, no allegations have been
made as against Zang in his personal capacity.  Accordingly, I order that
these claims (0611084 He Pei Huang and 0611082 Mei-Lin Tang) proceed only against
Wantell.   On the other four cases Judge Mondin adjourned (0509543
Han Ma, 0611939 Zhu Shu Lei, 0612042 Tao Huang, and 0611945 Yi Rong), the
pleadings and affidavits allege Zang made misrepresentations to the
Claimants.  I allow the addition of Zang as a Defendant on these four
claims as it is not plain and obvious that they do not disclose a reasonable
cause of action.

[
106
]
To summarize, in those cases where there is no basis upon which the Court could
find that Zang had any dealings with the Claimants other than strictly in his
capacity as President of Wantell and acting on behalf of Wantell, the
Applications to add Zang as a Defendant are dismissed.  Where the court
has previously ruled on Applications to add Zang and disallowed the amendments,
the claims will only be permitted to proceed against Wantell.  The six
cases in which the matters will go forward only as against Wantell are:
0611943 (Xue Mei Zheng); 0612173 (Miao Lian Zhang); 0509811 (Hua Zhang);
0611083 (Qun Yu); 0611084 (He Pei Huang); and 0611082 (Mei-Lin Tang).  As
set out above, the Court has ruled in favour of the remaining twenty cases and
disallows the Defendants’ applications to strike Zang as a Defendant.

In those cases where the Court has ruled in the Claimants’ favour to proceed

th
,
